newsitem.title: INDIA: India announces new royalty payment rates for oil.
newsitem.headline: India announces new royalty payment rates for oil.

text.p: The Indian government on Tuesday fixed royalty payments at the rate of 12.5 percent for onland and 10 percent for offshore oil under a New Exploration and Licensing Policy (NELP)
Royalty is paid by producing companies to the state or central government depending on who owns the resource.
Petroleum ministry officials said normally royalty on offshore finds goes to the centre while onshore royalty is received by India's state governments.

Junior Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu told parliament the government had approved the NELP aimed at boosting exploration efforts and giving more incentive to the private sector to invest in this critical area.

Balu said to encourage exploration in deep water and frontier areas, royalty will be charged at half the rate for offshore for areas beyond 400 metres bathymetry for the first seven years after commencement of commercial production.

Balu said upstream state-run firms like Oil and Natural Gas Corp. Ltd and Oil India Ltd would be provided a level playing field by giving them the same fiscal and contract terms as available to private firms.
"This will, inter alia, imply that oil companies including ONGC and OIL will be paid international prices of oil for discoveries made in the blocks offered under the new policy," Balu said.
But domestic oil firms will have to compete with the private sector for getting petroleum exploration licences instead of getting it on a nomination basis as at present, he said.

Under the NELP exploration blocks will be allotted on the basis of an open acreage system. This would mean that companies could apply for exploration blocks at any time and would not necessarily be restricted to bidding rounds.
India's demand for petroleum products is annually growing at over eight percent. The country is heavily dependent on imports to meet the demand.
Balu said at the current levels of projection of demand and supply, India's self-sufficiency was expected to decline to about 35 percent over the next five years from the present 50 percent.
Only six of the 26 basins in the country with potential for oil and gas have so far been explored.

Balu said ONGC and OIL would be exempted from payment of customs duty on import of goods needed for exploration and exploitation operations under the new policy to bring them on par with private companies who enjoy this facility.

The petroleum minister said there would be no compulsory state participation for exploration through ONGC and OIL and it would be up to the private companies to form strategic alliances with these companies if they so wished.
"There will be freedom to the contractors to market the crude oil and gas discovered in the blocks under the new policy in its doemstic market," Balu said.
He said government proposed to abolish cess payments for blocks offered under the new policy.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had in his 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget announced the highlights of the new policy. Balu's Tuesday statement gave more details.
